- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.3) — model fails to capture downward momentum, often lagging by 1–3 days.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term volatility, then overcorrects in subsequent periods.
- After a price spike, model forecasts a prolonged upward trend, but true price often corrects sharply within 5–7 days — especially if sentiment turns negative.
- Forecast horizon 30d is overly optimistic in early stages of a downtrend — model fails to recognize sentiment-driven reversal signals.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.67), model tends to average out, missing sharp directional shifts.
- Model underweights sentiment in early forecast windows — sentiment spikes are not reflected in initial 5–7 day forecasts.
